# Results — Study 342 (BDC-Yield) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One question — does **BIZD**
(VanEck BDC Income ETF), with its **~10% headline distribution yield**, survive credit
cycles, or is the yield partly a return of your own capital with a crash bolted on? — run
on the **total-return** tapes against **SPY** (equity) and **IEF** (7-10y Treasuries).
As-of **2026-05-31** (last complete month; the partial June 2026 bar is dropped). Match
the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

BIZD lists **2013-02-12**, which bounds the joint window honestly — and means BDCs' first
real stress test on this tape was the 2020 COVID crash and the 2022 credit-spread
widening, not the GFC.

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| **Joint panel (BIZD, SPY, IEF, total return)** | 2013-02-12 → 2026-05-29 | 3,344 | `1773bea09c5d` |

## The three arms — total return, 2013–2026

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (raw) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **BIZD (BDCs)** | **6.21%** | **20.1%** | 0.401 | **−55.4%** |
| SPY (equity) | 14.81% | 16.9% | 0.903 | −33.7% |
| IEF (7-10y Treasuries) | 1.32% | 6.5% | 0.235 | −23.9% |

BIZD's **volatility (20.1%) is *higher* than the S&P 500's** and its worst drawdown
(**−55.4%**) is far deeper, yet its total return (6.21% CAGR) is **well below** equities.
You bear *more* than equity risk for *less* than equity reward. *(Sharpe is raw — there is
no part-cash leg here, so all three arms race on the same footing; label is honest.)*

## The headline-yield illusion

| | Value |
|---|--:|
| Quoted distribution yield (headline) | **~10.0%** |
| Realised **total-return** CAGR | **6.21%** |
| Gap (phantom yield) | **3.79 pts** — **38% of the headline** |

Roughly **two-fifths of the advertised ~10% never became wealth**: it leaks out through
NAV erosion, fees on a leveraged book, return of capital, and crash losses chewing through
the carry. A distribution rate is not an earned yield.

## Who does BIZD actually move with?

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Full-sample beta of BIZD to **SPY** | **+0.722** (HAC *t* = **+5.48**) |
| Full-sample beta of BIZD to **IEF** | −0.241 (HAC *t* = −2.45) |
| **Downside** beta to SPY (worst 10% of SPY days) | **+1.10** |
| Correlation BIZD/SPY · BIZD/IEF | positive · negative |

BIZD loads on **equities, not bonds** (beta +0.72 to SPY, *negative* to Treasuries), and
on the worst 10% of equity days its downside beta to stocks is **above 1** — it falls
*more than the market* when the market falls hardest. The equity-comovement is robust to
autocorrelation (HAC *t* = **+5.48**, well clear of 2). → Signal **REAL**: BIZD is levered
equity, not a steady income sleeve.

## The decisive test — every >10% equity crash

Did BIZD cushion (rise, like a bond) or pile on (fall, like levered equity)?

| Equity drawdown | SPY | BIZD | IEF |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2015-07 → 2016-02 | −13.0% | **−18.1%** | +7.4% |
| 2018-01 → 2018-02 | −10.1% | −5.0% | −1.2% |
| 2018-09 → 2018-12 | −19.3% | −15.4% | +3.4% |
| 2020-02 → 2020-03 (COVID) | −33.7% | **−55.0%** | +6.4% |
| 2022-01 → 2022-10 | −24.5% | −15.8% | −15.4% |
| 2025-02 → 2025-04 | −18.8% | −19.6% | +2.7% |

**BIZD fell in 6 of 6 equity crashes; bonds (IEF) rose in 4 of 6.** In COVID it lost
**−55.0%** — *far more than the S&P 500's −33.7%* — exactly when its "income" was supposed
to be safe, while Treasuries gained +6.4%. The 10% yield is no cushion at all when credit
cracks; it is the trapdoor.

## How to read it

- **The levered-equity crash risk is real.** BIZD's beta to equities is +0.72 (HAC *t*
  5.48), >1 in the tail; it fell in every one of six equity crashes and lost more than
  stocks in COVID. → Signal **REAL**.
- **The "10% income" is the mirage.** Only ~6.2% of it survived as total return (38% is
  phantom), and it came with vol *above* equities and a *deeper* drawdown — for a
  *lower* return than just owning the S&P. As a high-yield income sleeve it does not
  survive contact with a credit cycle. → Tradability **MIRAGE**.
- **"Does the ~10% yield survive credit cycles?" → BUSTED.** A high distribution rate on a
  leveraged private-credit book is not bond-like income. In the only regime where it
  matters — the crash — BIZD behaved like levered equity, losing more than stocks.
